title: In-Place Vector Mutation
goal: Modify elements in a vector directly without reallocating.

sections.text: Vector mutation in other languages often uses index assignment in loops. In Rust, direct index assignment inside a loop repeatedly checks bounds and can conflict with borrowing rules.

sections.caption: &mut iterates mutable references to elements.

sections.text: Iterating over `&mut nums` yields a mutable reference to each element. Dereference with `*x` to modify the actual value inside the vector.
To remove elements based on a condition, use `retain` instead of calling `remove` inside a loop. Calling `remove` while looping shifts indices and causes borrow conflicts.

sections.code:
let mut nums = vec![1, 2, 3, 4];
nums.retain(|x| x % 2 == 0);
sections.caption: retain keeps elements matching the predicate.

sections.text: Modifying elements with mutable references and `retain` avoids extra vector allocations.

explanation: Modify elements in a vector directly without reallocating.
